subject: Announcement crediting & logo usage — order form redlines
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Announcement crediting & logo usage — order form redlines

Hi Elena / Legal team,

Thanks again for moving quickly on the order form. Attached is our latest draft (rishi_orderform_draft_v3.docx) — I highlighted the publicity section we usually include for pilots and joint announcements. Quick summary of the asks from our side: 
- We want the ability to reference Stellar Labs as a customer in blog posts and short case-study excerpts (1-2 sentences)
- Use of Stellar Labs logo on our customer page and co-branded one-pagers
- We will always send the final quote/press copy for review before publication

Two quick questions so we can update the order form before sending to procurement/legal on your side: 
1) Is a standard pre-approval window of 5 business days acceptable for Stellar?
2) Any internal rules on logo usage (artwork, size, full color vs grayscale) we should bake into the order form?

If helpful, we can accept tighter language: require Stellar approval for any public quote, and restrict logo to one co-branded asset unless you grant broader permission in writing.

Appreciate any redline guidance — happy to hop on a 20-minute call if it's easier.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Hi Rishi — thanks for the draft. Our legal team attached a marked-up copy with a few constraints that are pretty standard for us. Highlights from legal: 
- They want press mentions limited to product-level announcements related to the engagement; no blanket endorsement language.
- All quotes attributed to Stellar must be pre-approved and we request a "single author" policy for quoted text (we supply the final approved wording).
- Logo use: limited to co-branded marketing materials shared with customers and partner pages; no use on advertising or homepage banners without separate approval.
- Publicity approvals: 7 business days for legal review (they cited internal procurement timelines).
- They asked for SOC 2 Type II evidence before any public announcement referencing security posture.

See attached: Redlines_Stellar_OrderForm_0511.pdf — legal redlined the publicity & confidentiality sections and added a short clause about authorship control.

Happy to discuss trade-offs but legal is firm on authorship and the SOC2 requirement for anything that references security.

Best,
Elena
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Stellar Labs
[Attachment: Redlines_Stellar_OrderForm_0511.pdf]

Thanks Elena — and thanks for the redlines. Quick internal note for the thread and Kim / Legal: 

Summary of Stellar asks (from their redline):
- 7 business days for publicity approvals
- Strict authorship: Stellar supplies final quote wording and we cannot claim they "endorsed" our product beyond factual statements
- SOC2 Type II evidence before referencing security or controls
- Logo limited to co-branded one-pagers / partner pages; no homepage or ads without separate approval

Options I see from a commercial perspective: 
1) Accept their language as-is and add a small commercial concession (one-time pilot discount) — fastest path to signature.
2) Push for 5 business days & retain the ability to publish a short, factual success blurb (no endorsement phrasing).
3) Agree to authorship but request a pre-approved boilerplate Stellar can sign once to speed approvals for future customers.

Kim — can you confirm whether the SOC2 ask is a gating technical evidence requirement for a pilot mention or if we can offer a mitigated alternative (e.g., we can provide a security summary and commit to furnishing SOC2 within X days)? Also, please review the attached quick highlights I pulled from the PDF.

Rishi — I'm fine with option 2 if legal thinks the 5 business day window and tightened language are safe. If legal prefers option 1 we should think about a small concession to move the deal.

Laura
Head of Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redline_highlights_0511.md]

Subject: Re: Announcement crediting & logo usage — order form redlines

Laura / Rishi — thanks for the clear summary. Legal guidance below; happy to iterate on wording.

1) SOC2 ask — treat as material only for statements referencing security posture. Recommended approach: allow the parties to make factual statements about the engagement ("Redwood provided X to Stellar Labs for Y") without referencing security controls. Add a clause: "Any references to Stellar's security posture or controls require prior provision of SOC 2 Type II report or mutually agreed security addendum." That keeps the pilot announcement moving while protecting both sides.

2) Approval window — 5 business days is reasonable operationally; if Stellar is firm on 7, we can accept 7 for this agreement but add language for an accelerated approval process for future case studies ("Stellar may issue a standing pre-approval for up to N boilerplate quotes").

3) Authorship & endorsement — we should accept authorship control for direct quotes. Add a reciprocal sentence: "Neither party shall use the other party's name or logos in a manner that implies endorsement, partnership beyond the scope of the Agreement, or any statement about financial performance."

4) Logo usage — add a simple schedule: permitted uses (co-branded one-pagers, partner directory) and prohibited uses (homepage hero banners, paid ads) plus an approval flow: submit asset -> Stellar has 5 business days to approve -> deemed approved if no response (only if Stellar agrees to deemed approval; otherwise leave no-deem). If Stellar will not accept deemed approval, we should keep the 7 business day window.

Suggested redline snippet to add to Order Form / MSA publicity clause: 
"Publicity: Subject to prior written approval (not to be unreasonably withheld), Redwood may identify Stellar Labs as a customer and use Stellar Labs' logo in co-branded materials. Any quote attributed to Stellar Labs must be pre-approved in writing. References to Stellar Labs' security posture or controls require provision of SOC 2 Type II report or mutually agreed security addendum. Neither party may use the other's name or logos in marketing that implies endorsement beyond the scope of this Agreement."

Commercial recommendation: accept 7 business days for this order form to keep momentum; ask for a one-time pilot concession if Stellar insists on absolute no-deem approval.

I'll incorporate the language and send a redline back to Elena if you want me to.

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: suggested_publicity_snippet.txt]
